content.text:
The primary failure is an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade in the OAuth challenge.

MCPJam correctly connects to:

```text
https://mcp-local.skillplane.dev/mcp
```

But Skillplane responds with:

```text
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="http://mcp-local.skillplane.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"
```

Hosted MCPJam rejects that HTTP metadata URL with “Only HTTPS targets are allowed in hosted mode.”

I reproduced the Host-dependent behavior:

- Request through `127.0.0.1:5701` → challenge contains `https://...`
- Same request with `Host: mcp-local.skillplane.dev` → challenge contains `http://...`

Your `.dev.vars` and metadata endpoint are already correctly configured for HTTPS. The tunnel-preserved Host is triggering the local Wrangler proxy behavior.

Update the MCP ingress in [.data/cloudflared.yml](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/skillplane/.data/cloudflared.yml:6):

```yaml
- hostname: mcp-local.skillplane.dev
  service: http://127.0.0.1:5701
  originRequest:
    httpHostHeader: 127.0.0.1:5701
```

Then restart `pnpm local:tunnel` and verify:

```bash
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://mcp-local.skillplane.dev/mcp \
  | rg -i 'www-authenticate'
```

The header must contain:

```text
resource_metadata="https://mcp-local.skillplane.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"
```

Then reconnect MCPJam using exactly:

```text
https://mcp-local.skillplane.dev/mcp
```

The repeated `401` responses are expected before OAuth. The apple-touch-icon `404` is irrelevant.

There is also a secondary browser-CORS issue: `OPTIONS /mcp` currently gets authenticated and returns `401` because the `/mcp` handler authenticates before checking the HTTP method in [mcp/src/index.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/skillplane/mcp/src/index.ts:515). Hosted MCPJam’s proxy may avoid that, but if it becomes the next blocker, `/mcp` needs an unauthenticated CORS preflight handler before authentication.

No files were changed.
